title: Sell Mineral Rights in Emery County, UT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Emery County, UT | Coal & CBM
metaDescription: Own coal, CBM, or oil and gas minerals under Emery County and the San Rafael Swell? Get a documented, no-pressure offer from an active Utah mineral buyer.
heroLead: Emery County wraps around the San Rafael Swell, and the mineral estate here runs from deep underground coal seams to the shallow gas that seeps out of the same rock.
intro: Emery County, Utah, with Castle Dale as its county seat, sits on some of the thickest bituminous coal reserves in the Rocky Mountain region, and the towns strung along Highway 10 — Huntington, Ferron, Cleveland, Elmo, Clawson — grew up around mining and, later, mine-mouth power generation. Underneath the surface, mineral ownership is often a patchwork: coal rights severed from oil and gas rights, state trust sections interspersed with private and federal minerals, and family interests that trace back to homestead-era patents no one has looked at closely in fifty years.

We buy mineral, royalty, and non-participating royalty interests throughout Emery County, whether your income comes from an active coalbed-methane well, a coal lease royalty, or a conventional oil and gas unit tied to the county's edges near the San Rafael Swell and Green River. We will look at your actual deed and production history and tell you what we can offer in writing before you commit to anything.

sections.heading: Coal country economics and how they shape mineral value
paragraphs: Emery County's coal seams run thick and continuous, which historically supported large longwall mining operations and, more recently, coalbed methane wells that produce gas from the same coal without full-scale mining. For a mineral owner, that means your interest could be generating royalty from a coal lease, a CBM well, or both, depending on what part of the county your tract sits in and what the operator has developed. Interests near Huntington and Cleveland, close to the mine-mouth power plants, have historically seen more sustained development interest than more remote tracts near the Swell.

Because coal royalty terms were often set decades ago under older lease forms, the royalty rate on a legacy coal interest can look different — sometimes lower, sometimes structured on a per-ton rather than percentage basis — than what you would see on a modern oil and gas lease. We read the actual lease language tied to your interest rather than assuming a standard rate, because assuming wrong is how sellers get shortchanged or overvalue what they hold.

sections.heading: The San Rafael Swell and shallower conventional production
paragraphs: The San Rafael Swell is a striking geologic uplift that exposes rock layers across a huge span of the county, and along its margins there has been shallower conventional oil and gas activity distinct from the deep coal basin to the north. Owners with interests near Green River or the Swell's eastern flank may hold acreage tied to older vertical wells with a long, slow decline rather than the newer horizontal development pattern common elsewhere in the Uinta Basin. That distinction matters for valuation — an old, steady well with decades of production history is a different asset than a recently drilled unit still in its early decline.

If your family's interest sits in this part of the county, we will confirm which well or unit it is actually tied to before quoting, because 'Emery County oil and gas' covers a wide range of well types and ages, and treating them all the same would shortchange one owner and overpay another.

sections.heading: State trust land and fractionated family ownership
paragraphs: Like much of central Utah, Emery County has a substantial checkerboard of SITLA state trust sections interspersed with private and federal minerals, a legacy of the original railroad and school-trust grants. Production units frequently pool acreage across several ownership types, which can make a division order statement look more complicated than a simple private lease — but it does not diminish what your fractional share is worth, it just means confirming the pooling order takes a bit more courthouse and DOGM work on our end.

We also regularly work with Emery County owners whose interest has been divided among siblings or cousins through inheritance, sometimes without a clean probate ever being completed. We can help identify what share you actually hold and make an offer on that share specifically, without requiring the rest of the family to participate.

sections.heading: What to expect if you sell
paragraphs: We start with your legal description, deed, or division order, confirm the coal-versus-oil-and-gas severance and current producing status against Emery County Recorder and DOGM records, and send a written offer showing how we arrived at the number. If you accept, we prepare the mineral deed and manage recording and closing, typically within two to four weeks for a clean title file.

As with any coal-heavy county, we will flag if your specific tract has a title complication that needs curing before we can close, and we would rather tell you that upfront than surprise you later. Talk to your CPA before finalizing a sale about how the proceeds are taxed relative to continuing to receive royalty income — that decision depends on your broader financial picture, not only the mineral interest itself.

faqs.question: Is coal royalty valued the same way as oil and gas royalty?
faqs.answer: No. Coal leases are often structured differently, sometimes per-ton rather than percentage-of-value, so we read your specific lease terms before quoting rather than assuming a standard oil and gas rate applies.

faqs.question: My family's interest is near the San Rafael Swell — is that the same play as the coal country around Huntington?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. That area often ties to older, shallower conventional oil and gas rather than the deep coal seams further north, so we confirm exactly which well or unit your interest is tied to before making an offer.

faqs.question: We have a SITLA-adjacent interest with a complicated division order. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is common in Emery County. It takes extra confirmation work on our end but does not change your underlying ownership or our ability to make an offer.

faqs.question: What if the interest has been split among several heirs with no formal probate?
faqs.answer: We can help identify what share is actually yours and make an offer on it specifically, without needing the whole family to act together first.

faqs.question: How quickly can a sale close?
faqs.answer: Clean single-owner files typically close in two to four weeks. Coal-severance or heirship title issues can add time, and we will tell you upfront if that applies to your file.
